items.title: Divorce
items.heroTitle: Divorce Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Guiding you through contested and uncontested divorce with clarity, strategy, and steady advocacy.

sections.heading: Understanding Divorce in Texas
paragraphs: Texas is a no-fault divorce state, which means you can end your marriage simply on the ground of "insupportability" — that the marriage has become insupportable due to conflict of personalities. You do not have to prove your spouse did anything wrong. Texas law also recognizes fault grounds such as cruelty, adultery, abandonment, felony conviction, and living apart for at least three years, which can influence how property is divided.
To file for divorce in Texas, at least one spouse must have lived in the state for the preceding six months and in the county of filing for the preceding 90 days.

sections.heading: Contested vs. Uncontested Divorce
paragraphs: An uncontested divorce is one in which both spouses agree on all major issues — property division, debts, conservatorship, possession, and support. These cases are generally faster and less expensive. A contested divorce arises when spouses cannot agree on one or more issues, requiring negotiation, mediation, or a decision by the court. We handle both, and we work to resolve matters amicably wherever possible while remaining fully prepared to litigate.

sections.heading: The 60-Day Waiting Period
paragraphs: Texas imposes a mandatory minimum waiting period of 60 days from the date the divorce petition is filed before a court can finalize the divorce. Uncontested cases may be finalized shortly after this window closes, while contested matters involving children or complex assets can take several months or longer.

sections.heading: Dividing the Community Estate
paragraphs: Texas is a community property state. Most property and debt acquired during the marriage belongs to the community estate and is subject to division. The standard is not automatically 50/50 — courts divide the estate in a manner that is "just and right," considering factors such as each spouse's earning capacity, fault in the breakup, and who will have primary care of the children. Separate property, such as assets owned before marriage or received by gift or inheritance, is not divided.

sections.heading: Spousal Maintenance
paragraphs: Court-ordered spousal maintenance is limited in Texas. A spouse may qualify when they lack sufficient property to meet minimum reasonable needs and the marriage lasted at least 10 years, or where there is a history of family violence or a disability. The amount and duration of maintenance are capped by statute.

sections.heading: Divorce Involving Children
paragraphs: When children are involved, the divorce will also establish conservatorship (custody), possession and access (visitation), and child support. Every decision affecting the children is guided by the best interest of the child standard. We help parents protect their relationship with their children while building a workable, court-approved parenting plan.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: We provide steady guidance from the first filing to the final decree. Attorney Sehar Hirani takes the time to understand your goals, explains your options in plain language, and builds a strategy shaped around your family, timeline, and finances — so you can move forward with confidence.

items.title: Child Custody
items.heroTitle: Child Custody Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Protecting your relationship with your children through every stage of a custody matter.

sections.heading: Custody Is Called Conservatorship in Texas
paragraphs: Texas law does not use the word "custody." Instead, it refers to "conservatorship," which describes a parent's legal rights and duties regarding a child, and "possession and access," which describes the schedule of when each parent has the child. Understanding this distinction is important, because a parent can have significant decision-making rights even when the other parent has primary physical possession.

sections.heading: Joint vs. Sole Managing Conservatorship
paragraphs: Texas courts presume that appointing both parents as joint managing conservators is in the child's best interest. This does not mean equal time — it means both parents share rights and duties such as decisions about education, medical care, and religious upbringing. A court may appoint one parent as sole managing conservator when there is a history of family violence, neglect, substance abuse, or absence.

sections.heading: Possession and Access (Visitation)
paragraphs: The Texas Family Code provides a Standard Possession Order (SPO) that is presumed to be in the best interest of children age three and older when parents live within 100 miles of each other. It typically gives the non-primary parent possession on the first, third, and fifth weekends of the month, Thursday evenings, alternating holidays, and extended summer possession. Schedules can be customized to fit a family's needs.

sections.heading: The Best Interest of the Child Standard
paragraphs: Every custody decision in Texas is guided by the best interest of the child. Courts weigh factors including each parent's ability to care for the child, the stability of each home, the child's emotional and physical needs, any history of family violence, and — for older children — the child's own preferences. Texas law prohibits courts from favoring a parent based on gender.

sections.heading: Modifying a Custody Order
paragraphs: Custody orders can be modified when there has been a material and substantial change in circumstances since the last order and the change would serve the child's best interest. Common reasons include a parent's relocation, a change in a child's needs, or concerns about the child's safety or well-being in the current arrangement.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: We know how much is at stake in a custody case. We build a clear, evidence-based case focused on your child's best interest, prepare you thoroughly for mediation and hearings, and fight to protect your role in your child's life.

items.title: Child Support
items.heroTitle: Child Support Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Establishing, enforcing, and modifying fair child support under Texas guidelines.

sections.heading: How Child Support Is Calculated in Texas
paragraphs: Texas uses statutory guidelines based on the paying parent's net monthly resources and the number of children before the court. The guideline percentages generally begin at 20% of net resources for one child and increase with each additional child. Net resources include wages, self-employment income, and many other sources, minus certain deductions such as taxes and the cost of the child's health insurance.

sections.heading: Deviating From the Guidelines
paragraphs: A court can order more or less than the guideline amount when the evidence shows it is in the child's best interest. Factors include the child's special needs, the amount of time each parent has possession, educational expenses, and the financial circumstances of both parents. There is also a cap on the portion of net resources to which the guideline percentages automatically apply.

sections.heading: Medical and Dental Support
paragraphs: In addition to base child support, Texas orders require provision for the child's health and dental insurance. The court will allocate responsibility for premiums and uninsured medical costs between the parents.

sections.heading: Enforcing a Child Support Order
paragraphs: When a parent fails to pay court-ordered support, Texas provides powerful enforcement tools, including wage withholding, interception of tax refunds, suspension of driver's and professional licenses, liens, and contempt of court — which can carry fines and jail time. We help parents pursue the support their children are owed.

sections.heading: Modifying Child Support
paragraphs: Child support can be modified when there has been a material and substantial change in circumstances, such as a significant change in either parent's income, or when three years have passed since the last order and the guideline amount would differ by a set threshold. Support is not automatically adjusted — a modification must be requested.

sections.heading: How Long Support Lasts
paragraphs: In Texas, child support generally continues until the child turns 18 or graduates from high school, whichever is later. Support may continue indefinitely for a child with a disability that requires substantial care and supervision.

items.title: Adoption
items.heroTitle: Adoption Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Helping Texas families grow through stepparent, relative, and adult adoptions.

sections.heading: A Joyful but Detailed Process
paragraphs: Adoption is one of the most rewarding areas of family law — but it is also one of the most procedurally detailed. Texas law requires careful compliance with statutory steps, from termination of prior parental rights to home studies and the final adoption hearing. Having experienced guidance helps ensure nothing delays your family's future together.

sections.heading: Stepparent Adoption
paragraphs: Stepparent adoption is one of the most common adoptions we handle. It allows a stepparent to become the legal parent of their spouse's child. In most cases, the rights of the other biological parent must first be terminated — either voluntarily or by court order — before the adoption can be finalized.

sections.heading: Terminating Parental Rights
paragraphs: Because a child can have only two legal parents, an adoption generally requires that the rights of an existing parent be terminated first. Termination may be voluntary, through a signed affidavit of relinquishment, or involuntary, based on statutory grounds such as abandonment or endangerment. This is often the most sensitive part of an adoption case.

sections.heading: Home Studies and Background Checks
paragraphs: Texas typically requires a social study (home study) and criminal background checks for adoptions. The court wants to confirm that the adoptive placement serves the child's best interest. We help families prepare for and navigate these requirements smoothly.

sections.heading: Adult Adoption
paragraphs: Texas also permits the adoption of an adult, which can formalize a lifelong parent-child relationship and carry inheritance and other legal benefits. Adult adoption is generally a more streamlined process because parental rights and consent issues are not involved.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: We handle each step — petitions, terminations, home studies, and the final hearing — so your family can focus on what matters. We are honored to help clients complete their families and are with you through to the final decree of adoption.

items.title: Father's Rights
items.heroTitle: Father's Rights Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Defending fathers who want to remain present and active in their children's lives.

sections.heading: Texas Law Does Not Favor Mothers
paragraphs: A common misconception is that Texas courts automatically favor mothers in custody matters. In fact, Texas law expressly prohibits courts from considering a parent's gender when deciding conservatorship and possession. Fathers have the same rights and standing as mothers, and courts decide based on the best interest of the child.

sections.heading: Establishing Paternity
paragraphs: For unmarried fathers, establishing legal paternity is the essential first step to securing parental rights. Paternity can be established by signing an Acknowledgment of Paternity or through a court order, often supported by genetic testing. Until paternity is established, an unmarried father may have no legal right to possession or decision-making.

sections.heading: Securing Meaningful Possession Time
paragraphs: We help fathers obtain fair and meaningful possession schedules — whether that is a Standard Possession Order, an expanded schedule, or, where appropriate, equal or primary possession. The goal is to protect the father's ongoing, active role in the child's daily life.

sections.heading: Rights and Duties as a Conservator
paragraphs: Being named a joint managing conservator gives a father important rights, such as access to medical and school records and a voice in decisions about the child's education, health care, and upbringing. We fight to make sure those rights are recognized and enforced.

sections.heading: Defending Against Unfair Allegations
paragraphs: Fathers sometimes face unfounded allegations designed to limit their access. We help fathers respond effectively, present evidence, and protect their reputation and their relationship with their children.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: Attorney Sehar Hirani is passionate about defending fathers who want to remain committed and involved. We build strong, child-focused cases and advocate tirelessly for a father's right to parent.

items.title: Conservatorship
items.heroTitle: Conservatorship Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Clarifying parental rights, duties, and decision-making for your children.

sections.heading: What Conservatorship Means
paragraphs: In Texas, conservatorship defines the legal rights and duties a parent holds regarding a child — including the right to make decisions about education, medical and psychological treatment, and religious upbringing, and the duty to care for and support the child. Conservatorship is distinct from possession and access, which governs the physical schedule.

sections.heading: Joint Managing Conservatorship
paragraphs: Texas courts presume that both parents should serve as joint managing conservators, sharing rights and duties. This arrangement encourages both parents to remain involved in major decisions. The order will specify which rights are shared, which are exclusive to one parent, and which each parent may exercise independently.

sections.heading: Sole Managing Conservatorship
paragraphs: In some cases, a court will appoint one parent as sole managing conservator, giving that parent the exclusive right to make certain key decisions. This is more likely where there is a history of family violence, neglect, substance abuse, or where a parent has been largely absent from the child's life.

sections.heading: Possessory Conservators
paragraphs: A parent who is not named a managing conservator may be named a possessory conservator, with a right to possession and access under a schedule set by the court. We help clients understand and structure the possession terms that fit their family.

sections.heading: Modifying Conservatorship
paragraphs: Conservatorship terms can be modified when circumstances change materially and substantially and modification serves the child's best interest. We assist parents seeking to adjust rights and duties as their family's needs evolve.

items.title: Modifications
items.heroTitle: Order Modification Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Updating custody, support, and possession orders when life changes.

sections.heading: When Orders Can Be Changed
paragraphs: Life does not stop after a family court order is signed. Texas law allows conservatorship, possession, and child support orders to be modified when there has been a material and substantial change in circumstances since the order was rendered, and the change is in the child's best interest.

sections.heading: Common Reasons to Modify
paragraphs: Frequent grounds for modification include a parent's relocation, a significant change in income, a change in the child's needs, a parent's remarriage, or concerns about the child's safety or well-being in the current arrangement. A child's own preference may also carry weight as the child gets older.

sections.heading: Modifying Custody and Possession
paragraphs: Changes to conservatorship or the possession schedule require showing that the modification benefits the child. Where the request is to change the parent who has the exclusive right to determine the child's primary residence within the first year of an order, Texas imposes additional requirements.

sections.heading: Modifying Child Support
paragraphs: Support can be modified when there is a material and substantial change — such as a job loss or a raise — or when three years have passed and the guideline amount would change by a set threshold. Support does not adjust automatically; a formal modification must be filed and granted.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: We evaluate whether your circumstances meet the legal standard for modification, gather the evidence needed to prove it, and pursue an updated order that reflects your family's current reality.

items.title: Enforcement & Contempt
items.heroTitle: Enforcement & Contempt Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Holding the other party accountable when a court order is ignored.

sections.heading: When a Party Violates a Court Order
paragraphs: A family court order is not a suggestion — it is a binding order of the court. When the other party refuses to pay support, denies you court-ordered possession, or ignores other terms, Texas law provides enforcement remedies to compel compliance and, where appropriate, punish the violation.

sections.heading: Enforcing Child Support
paragraphs: Unpaid child support can be enforced through wage withholding, liens, interception of tax refunds and lottery winnings, suspension of licenses, and a judgment for arrears with interest. In serious cases, a parent who willfully refuses to pay can be held in contempt of court.

sections.heading: Enforcing Possession and Access
paragraphs: When one parent denies the other court-ordered time with the children, the aggrieved parent can file an enforcement action. The court can order make-up possession time, impose fines, award attorney's fees, and hold the violating parent in contempt.

sections.heading: Contempt of Court
paragraphs: Contempt is a finding that a party willfully violated a clear and specific order they were able to obey. Penalties can include fines and even jail time. Because contempt carries serious consequences, these cases require precise pleading and proof, which is where experienced representation matters.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: We document violations carefully, draft enforcement pleadings that meet Texas's strict specificity requirements, and pursue the remedies that will restore compliance with your order.

items.title: Property Division
items.heroTitle: Property Division Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Protecting your fair share of the marital estate in a Texas divorce.

sections.heading: Community Property in Texas
paragraphs: Texas is a community property state. The law presumes that all property and debt acquired during the marriage is community property, owned equally by both spouses and subject to division in a divorce. Overcoming this presumption for a particular asset requires clear and convincing evidence that it is separate property.

sections.heading: Separate vs. Community Property
paragraphs: Separate property — which is not divided — includes assets owned before the marriage, and property received during the marriage by gift or inheritance, as well as certain personal injury recoveries. Careful tracing is often required to establish and protect a spouse's separate property claims.

sections.heading: A "Just and Right" Division
paragraphs: Texas courts do not automatically split the community estate 50/50. Instead, they divide it in a manner that is just and right, considering factors such as each spouse's earning capacity, education, health, fault in the breakup, and which parent will have primary care of the children.

sections.heading: Complex Assets
paragraphs: Property division often involves complex assets — retirement accounts and pensions (which may require a Qualified Domestic Relations Order), businesses, real estate, stock options, and significant debt. Proper valuation and characterization of these assets is essential to a fair outcome.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: We identify, characterize, and value the marital estate, protect your separate property, and advocate for a division that safeguards your financial future as you begin the next chapter.

items.title: Prenuptial Agreements
items.heroTitle: Prenuptial Agreement Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Thoughtful premarital agreements that protect both partners.

sections.heading: What a Prenuptial Agreement Does
paragraphs: A prenuptial agreement — sometimes called a premarital or "prenup" agreement — is a contract signed before marriage that defines how property and debts will be treated during the marriage and in the event of divorce or death. In a community property state like Texas, a well-drafted prenup lets couples set their own rules rather than relying on default law.

sections.heading: What It Can Cover
paragraphs: Texas allows premarital agreements to address the characterization of property as separate or community, the management of assets during marriage, the division of property upon divorce, and the disposition of property upon death. An agreement cannot adversely affect a child's right to support.

sections.heading: Making the Agreement Enforceable
paragraphs: To hold up in a Texas court, a premarital agreement must be in writing and signed voluntarily, with fair and reasonable disclosure of each party's finances (unless properly waived). Agreements signed under duress, or without disclosure, may be challenged. Independent legal counsel for each party strengthens enforceability.

sections.heading: Who Benefits From a Prenup
paragraphs: Prenuptial agreements are valuable for individuals entering a marriage with significant assets, a business, children from a prior relationship, or substantial debt — and for any couple who wants clarity and peace of mind about their financial future.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: We draft and review premarital agreements that are clear, fair, and built to withstand scrutiny — protecting both parties and reducing conflict should circumstances ever change.

items.title: Postnuptial Agreements
items.heroTitle: Postnuptial Agreement Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Clarifying property rights and expectations after you are married.

sections.heading: What a Postnuptial Agreement Does
paragraphs: A postnuptial agreement is a marital property agreement entered into after a couple is already married. In Texas, spouses can use partition and exchange agreements to convert community property into each spouse's separate property, and to define how future income and assets will be characterized.

sections.heading: Why Couples Use Them
paragraphs: Postnuptial agreements can bring clarity when circumstances change during a marriage — for example, when one spouse starts a business, receives an inheritance, or when the couple wants to define financial expectations to strengthen their marriage. They can also be part of resolving financial disagreements.

sections.heading: Requirements for Enforceability
paragraphs: Like premarital agreements, postnuptial agreements must be in writing and signed voluntarily, with fair disclosure of assets unless waived. Because spouses owe each other duties of fairness, these agreements are closely scrutinized, so careful drafting and full disclosure are essential.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: We prepare and review postnuptial agreements that accurately reflect your intentions and comply with Texas law, giving you and your spouse clarity and confidence about your financial arrangements.

items.title: Name Changes
items.heroTitle: Name Change Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Straightforward help with adult and minor name change petitions.

sections.heading: Legal Name Changes in Texas
paragraphs: Texas allows adults and minors to change their legal name through a court petition. While the process is often straightforward, it must be handled correctly to be recognized by government agencies, employers, and financial institutions. We help ensure your petition is complete and properly filed in the appropriate court.

sections.heading: Adult Name Changes
paragraphs: An adult may petition to change their name for many reasons — marriage, divorce, gender identity, or personal preference. Texas requires disclosure of certain background information, and the change must be in the person's interest and not for a fraudulent or unlawful purpose. Applicants with certain criminal histories face additional requirements.

sections.heading: Minor Name Changes
paragraphs: Changing a child's name generally requires the consent or notice of both parents and a finding that the change is in the child's best interest. These cases can be more sensitive, particularly when a parent objects, and benefit from experienced representation.

sections.heading: After the Order
paragraphs: Once the court grants a name change, we help you understand the follow-up steps — updating your Social Security record, driver's license, passport, and other important documents — so your new name is recognized everywhere it matters.

items.title: Auto Accidents
items.heroTitle: Auto Accident Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Fighting for full compensation for crash victims across Houston and Texas.

sections.heading: After a Car Accident, You Should Focus on Recovery
paragraphs: Every year, thousands of people in the Houston and Katy area are injured in auto accidents caused by someone else's negligence. In an instant, your life can be turned upside down — you may be dealing with painful injuries, mounting medical bills, lost income, and insurance companies more concerned with their bottom line than your recovery.

You deserve a powerful advocate in your corner. As your dedicated auto accident attorney, Hirani Law Firm works to hold negligent drivers accountable and secure the full and fair compensation you need to rebuild.

sections.heading: Common Causes of Serious Crashes
paragraphs: Many collisions are caused by preventable driver negligence — distracted driving and texting, speeding and reckless driving, drunk or drugged driving, and failure to yield at intersections. We investigate the cause of your crash and gather the evidence needed to prove the other driver was at fault.

sections.heading: Texas's Fault and Insurance Rules
paragraphs: Texas is an at-fault (tort) state, which means the driver responsible for a crash is responsible for the resulting damages. Texas also follows a modified comparative fault rule: you can recover damages as long as you are not more than 50% at fault, though your recovery is reduced by your share of fault. Insurance adjusters often try to shift blame to reduce what they pay — we push back.

sections.heading: Damages You May Recover
paragraphs: Depending on your case, you may be entitled to compensation for medical expenses (past and future), lost wages and loss of earning capacity, property damage, and non-economic damages such as pain and suffering, disfigurement, and loss of enjoyment of life.

sections.heading: The Deadline to File
paragraphs: In most Texas personal injury cases, you have two years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit. Missing this statute of limitations usually means losing your right to recover — so it is important to act promptly and preserve evidence early.

sections.heading: No Win, No Fee
paragraphs: We handle auto accident cases on a contingency fee basis. You pay us nothing up front, and we only get paid if we recover compensation for you. There is no financial risk to hiring us — just experienced advocacy focused on your recovery.

items.title: 18-Wheeler Accidents
items.heroTitle: 18-Wheeler Accident Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Representation for serious 18-wheeler and commercial truck accident claims.

sections.heading: Truck and Commercial Vehicle Accidents
paragraphs: Accidents involving 18-wheelers and commercial trucks are governed by federal regulations and often involve multiple liable parties. These are complex, high-stakes cases, and they demand an attorney with the experience to handle them.

Because of their size and weight, commercial trucks can cause catastrophic injuries. When your life has been turned upside down by a truck crash, you are dealing with serious injuries, large medical bills, and lost income — while the trucking company's insurers move quickly to protect themselves.

sections.heading: Federal Trucking Regulations
paragraphs: Commercial carriers and drivers must comply with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) regulations covering hours of service, driver qualifications, vehicle maintenance, and cargo loading. Violations — such as logbook falsifications or skipped inspections — can be powerful evidence of negligence. We know how to obtain and use these records.

sections.heading: Multiple Liable Parties
paragraphs: Unlike a typical car crash, a truck accident may involve several responsible parties: the driver, the trucking company, the vehicle's owner, a maintenance contractor, or the company that loaded the cargo. Identifying every liable party is critical to recovering full compensation, especially in cases involving severe injuries.

sections.heading: Preserving Crucial Evidence
paragraphs: Key evidence in a truck case — the electronic control module ("black box") data, driver logs, dispatch records, and the truck itself — can disappear if not preserved quickly. We act fast to send legal preservation notices and secure the evidence before it is lost or destroyed.

sections.heading: Damages in Truck Accident Cases
paragraphs: Victims may recover for past and future medical expenses, lost wages and lost earning capacity, pain and suffering, disfigurement, and property damage. In cases involving egregious conduct, punitive damages may also be available.

sections.heading: We Are Trial Lawyers
paragraphs: Trucking companies and their insurers know which attorneys are willing to go to trial and which are not. We prepare every case as if it will go before a jury, giving our clients maximum leverage in negotiations — and readiness for the courtroom if a fair settlement is not offered. And with our no win, no fee guarantee, you pay nothing unless we win.

items.title: Motorcycle Accidents
items.heroTitle: Motorcycle Accident Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Standing up for injured riders against biased insurance companies.

sections.heading: Riders Face Unfair Bias
paragraphs: Motorcyclists are among the most vulnerable people on the road, and they often face unfair bias from insurance companies and even other drivers who assume the rider was at fault. We fight against this bias and work to ensure motorcycle accident victims receive the full compensation they deserve.

sections.heading: Severe Injuries Are Common
paragraphs: Because riders have little protection in a crash, motorcycle accidents frequently cause catastrophic injuries — traumatic brain injuries, spinal cord damage, broken bones, and road rash requiring extensive treatment. These serious injuries mean higher medical costs and longer recoveries, which must be fully accounted for in any claim.

sections.heading: Proving the Other Driver's Negligence
paragraphs: Many motorcycle crashes happen because a driver failed to see the rider, violated the rider's right of way, or made an unsafe left turn. We investigate the scene, gather witness statements and available video, and build a clear case showing the other party's negligence.

sections.heading: Overcoming Comparative Fault Arguments
paragraphs: Insurers often argue that the rider was speeding or otherwise partly at fault to reduce their payout. Under Texas's modified comparative fault rule, you can still recover as long as you are not more than 50% at fault, though your recovery is reduced by your percentage. We work to minimize any unfair allocation of blame.

sections.heading: No Win, No Fee
paragraphs: We handle motorcycle accident cases on a contingency basis — you owe us nothing unless we recover for you. Our focus is on getting injured riders the compensation and respect they deserve.

items.title: Slip & Fall
items.heroTitle: Slip & Fall Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Premises liability claims against property owners who fail to keep people safe.

sections.heading: Premises Liability in Texas
paragraphs: Property owners and businesses have a legal duty to maintain reasonably safe conditions for people who are lawfully on their property. When they fail to fix or warn about a dangerous condition — a wet floor, uneven pavement, poor lighting, or a hidden hazard — and someone is injured, they may be held liable under Texas premises liability law.

sections.heading: Proving a Slip and Fall Case
paragraphs: To recover, an injured visitor generally must show that a dangerous condition existed, that the owner knew or should have known about it, that the owner failed to take reasonable steps to address it, and that this failure caused the injury. Evidence such as incident reports, surveillance footage, and witness statements is often critical — and can disappear quickly.

sections.heading: Your Status on the Property Matters
paragraphs: The duty a property owner owes depends on why you were there. Invitees — such as customers of a business — are owed the highest duty of care, while lesser duties apply to licensees and trespassers. Understanding your status is key to evaluating your claim.

sections.heading: Comparative Fault
paragraphs: Property owners frequently argue that the injured person was not watching where they were going. Under Texas's modified comparative fault rule, you can still recover as long as you were not more than 50% at fault, with your recovery reduced by your share. We work to defeat unfair blame-shifting.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: We move quickly to preserve evidence, establish the owner's knowledge of the hazard, and pursue compensation for your medical bills, lost income, and pain and suffering — all on a no win, no fee basis.

items.title: Workers' Compensation
items.heroTitle: Workplace Injury Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Help for injured workers facing denied benefits and disputed claims.

sections.heading: Injured on the Job in Texas
paragraphs: Texas is unique in that private employers are not required to carry workers' compensation insurance. Whether your employer is a "subscriber" (carries workers' comp) or a "non-subscriber" makes a significant difference in how you pursue compensation for a workplace injury. We help injured workers understand their rights and their best path forward.

sections.heading: Workers' Compensation Claims
paragraphs: If your employer carries workers' compensation, you may be entitled to benefits including medical care and a portion of your lost wages, regardless of fault. However, claims are frequently delayed or denied. We help workers file properly, appeal denials, and fight for the benefits they are owed.

sections.heading: Non-Subscriber Injury Claims
paragraphs: When an employer does not carry workers' compensation, an injured worker may bring a personal injury claim directly against the employer for negligence. Importantly, non-subscribing employers lose key legal defenses, which can strengthen an injured worker's case for full damages — including pain and suffering.

sections.heading: Third-Party Claims
paragraphs: Sometimes a workplace injury is caused by someone other than your employer — a negligent contractor, a property owner, or a defective product manufacturer. In those situations, you may have a separate third-party claim for additional compensation beyond any workers' comp benefits.

sections.heading: How Hirani Law Firm Helps
paragraphs: We evaluate your employer's coverage, identify every available source of compensation, and advocate for the medical care and financial recovery you need after a workplace injury — with no fee unless we win.
